title: Saturday Night Live
wiki_lead:
Saturday Night Live (SNL) is an American late-night live sketch comedy variety show created by Lorne Michaels and developed by Michaels and Dick Ebersol that airs on NBC and streams next day (along with a full catalogue) on Peacock. The show's premiere was hosted by George Carlin on NBC on October 11, 1975, under the original title NBC's Saturday Night. The show's comedy sketches are performed by a large and varying cast of repertory and newer “featured” cast members. Each episode is hosted by a celebrity guest, has a musical guest, and is broadcast live with a studio audience.
The host usually delivers a comedic monologue toward the start of the show and then performs in sketches with the cast, and introduces featured performances by a musical guest. An episode normally begins with a cold open sketch that is usually based on current political or pop cultural events and ends with someone breaking character and proclaiming, "Live from New York, it's Saturday Night!", before moving to credits and introduction of the guest host.
In 1980, Michaels left the show to explore other opportunities. He was replaced by Jean Doumanian, who was then replaced by Ebersol after a season of poor reviews. Ebersol ran the show until 1985, when Michaels returned. Since then, Michaels has served as showrunner. Many SNL cast members have found national stardom while appearing on the show, and achieved success in film and television, both in front of and behind the camera. Others associated with the show, such as writers, have gone on to successful careers creating, writing, and starring in television and film.
SNL is broadcast from Studio 8H at NBC's headquarters in 30 Rockefeller Plaza in New York. SNL has aired 1,014 episodes since its debut, making it one of the longest-running network television programs in the United States. The show format has been developed and recreated in several countries, meeting with different levels of success. Successful sketches have seen life outside the show as feature films, including The Blues Brothers (1980), Wayne's World (1992) and A Night at the Roxbury (1998). The show has been marketed in other ways, including home media releases of "best of" and whole seasons, and books and documentaries about behind-the-scenes activities of running and developing the show.
Throughout five decades on air, Saturday Night Live has received a vast number of awards, including 84 Primetime Emmy Awards, 6 Writers Guild of America Awards, and 3 Peabody Awards. In 2000, it was inducted into the National Association of Broadcasters Hall of Fame. It was ranked tenth in TV Guide's "50 Greatest TV Shows of All Time" list, and in 2007 it was listed as one of Time's "100 Best TV Shows of All-TIME". As of 2022, the show had received more than 305 Primetime Emmy Award nominations, the most received by any television program.

grok_lead: Saturday Night Live (SNL) is an American late-night live television sketch comedy and variety show created by Canadian producer Lorne Michaels that premiered on NBC on October 11, 1975, under the initial title NBC's Saturday Night. The program, broadcast weekly from Studio 8H in Rockefeller Center, New York City, typically features a celebrity guest host delivering a monologue, followed by a series of original comedic sketches parodying contemporary events and culture, interspersed with musical performances by a resident house band and guest artists. Over its 51 seasons as of 2026, with the 52nd season having premiered on September 26, 2026, SNL has maintained a format emphasizing improvisation, topical satire, and recurring characters performed by its ensemble cast, which rotates periodically to incorporate new talent. SNL has profoundly influenced American comedy by launching the careers of numerous performers, including early stars like Dan Aykroyd, John Belushi, and Gilda Radner, and later alumni such as Tina Fey, Amy Poehler, and Bill Hader, many of whom transitioned to film, television, and writing success. The show's live broadcast element, combined with its willingness to tackle controversial subjects, has made it a cultural staple, though it has faced periodic hiatuses and production challenges, including a brief overhaul in the early 1980s before Michaels' return in 1985. In February 2025 the program marked its 50th anniversary with a three-hour special that drew 14.8 million viewers, NBCâs most-watched primetime entertainment telecast in five years. Its defining characteristics include sharp political satire âoften skewering presidents and public figuresâwhich has generated both acclaim for boldness and criticism for perceived ideological slant favoring liberal viewpoints over balanced scrutiny. Among its notable achievements, SNL holds the record for the most Primetime Emmy Awards won by any show, with 114 victories as of 2026, including multiple wins for Outstanding Variety Sketch Series, eight for the 2025 SNL50 anniversary special, and production categories. Controversies have marked its history, from on-air protests like SinÃ©ad O'Connor's 1992 tearing of a papal photo, leading to her ban from the show, to ongoing debates over uneven satirical treatment of political parties, where empirical tallies of sketches reveal heavier focus on conservative targets amid mainstream media's own left-leaning tendencies that may amplify rather than contextualize such patterns.
